terms.meaning: the language that tells a web page how things should look, such as colour, size and spacing
the part of a CSS rule that says which elements the style applies to
a named colour or value, such as the background colour, that many rules can reuse
a rule that applies only when the screen is a certain width or a user setting is on
the screen width at which the layout changes, such as 860 pixels
a set of colours for light or dark appearance

sections.name: :root
sections.title: Default light colours and base settings
sections.what: Sets the shared colour palette, font, corner rounding and phone safe-area padding for the whole app. Light appearance is the default.
sections.why: Likely reason: defining colours once lets every part of the app share them.
sections.watch_out: Many colours are set again in the dark blocks, so a change here alone may not appear in dark mode.

sections.name: :root[data-theme="dark"] (part 1)
sections.title: Dark theme colours and base page styles
sections.what: Applies the dark palette when the page is marked dark, and sets base text, buttons, focus outlines and the layout of the side menu and main area.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the app look right in dark mode, selected by the user or the system.
sections.watch_out: The side menu and main area use fixed pixel widths here, so narrow screens depend on the later size rules.

sections.name: :root[data-theme="dark"] (part 2)
sections.title: Document previews, status flags and gauge styles
sections.what: Styles the fake document thumbnails, small status flags, task cards, the gauge legend and the bar chart.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: :root[data-theme="dark"] (part 3)
sections.title: Map, floating panel and layer control styles
sections.what: Styles the map area, its zoom and layer buttons, the floating info panel with its small bar sparkline, and the differences card.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: A later rule hides the layer buttons entirely, so any change to them will not appear.

sections.name: :root[data-theme="dark"] (part 4)
sections.title: Home page hero and list styles
sections.what: Lays out the home page hero with its heading, text and buttons, plus its fade-in animation, blurred backdrop, numbered steps and check lists.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives the home page a large, animated first screen.
sections.watch_out: Hero text stays hidden until the revealed class is added by page code, so a missing class leaves the text invisible.

sections.name: :root[data-theme="dark"] (part 5)
sections.title: Opening document card and map pins
sections.what: Styles the folded document cover that opens to show a map and parchment panels, the map pins, the pop-up card, satellite thumbnails and the short toast message.
sections.why: Likely reason: decorative open-document effect on the parcel page.
sections.watch_out: The opening animation depends on page code adding the open and settled classes, so without them the cover stays shut.

sections.name: :root[data-theme="dark"] (part 6)
sections.title: Footer text style
sections.what: Sets the small grey footer text and its padding.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: @media (max-width:1100px)
sections.title: Medium screen layout changes
sections.what: On screens up to 1100 pixels wide, changes card widths so they fit better and makes the map a little shorter.
sections.why: Likely reason: to fit tablets and small laptops.

sections.name: @media (max-width:700px)
sections.title: Phone layout changes
sections.what: On screens up to 700 pixels wide, switches to a single column, makes cards full width, moves the map info panel to the bottom and turns off motion for users who ask for less motion.
sections.why: Likely reason: small screens cannot fit the wide layout.
sections.watch_out: The reduced motion rule switches off every transition, so animations will not run for those users.

sections.name: @media (max-width:860px)
sections.title: Compact top bar and bottom navigation
sections.what: On screens up to 860 pixels wide, makes the top bar compact, hides the long notice, moves the side menu to a floating bar at the bottom and shows a small logo.
sections.why: Likely reason: small screens lack room for a side menu.
sections.watch_out: The notice text is hidden on small screens, so anything shown only there is missing on phones.

sections.name: @media (min-width:861px)
sections.title: Side menu on wide screens
sections.what: On wider screens, shows the side menu as a rounded floating card in a narrow left column.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps navigation visible on desktops.
sections.watch_out: This block and the one above it switch at the same 860 pixel boundary, so changes to one must match the other.

sections.name: @media (max-width:860px)
sections.title: Hero and notice tweaks for tablets and phones
sections.what: On screens up to 860 pixels, adjusts the home hero height and the small notice box.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .case-layout
sections.title: Two-column case page layout
sections.what: Lays out case pages with a fixed 210 pixel navigation column beside a flexible content column.
sections.why: Likely reason: case pages keep a side menu next to the content.

sections.name: @media (max-width: 860px)
sections.title: Single column case pages on small screens
sections.what: On screens up to 860 pixels, stacks the case navigation above the content.
sections.why: Likely reason: small screens cannot fit two columns.

sections.name: .case-content
sections.title: Spacing of case content sections
sections.what: Stacks the case content sections vertically with even spacing and lets them shrink without overflowing.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .case-nav
sections.title: Case navigation panel
sections.what: Styles the case navigation box with a light translucent background, padding and rounded corners.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .case-nav a
sections.title: Case navigation link styles
sections.what: Makes each navigation link a padded block with a quick colour change. The active link is grouped with the hover style.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The active link and the hovered link share one look, so the current page looks the same as a link under the mouse.

sections.name: .case-nav a:hover
sections.title: Lime highlight on navigation hover
sections.what: When the mouse moves over a navigation link, it turns lime green with bold text.
sections.why: Likely reason: clear feedback that a link can be clicked.

sections.name: .case-header
sections.title: Case header and grouped content boxes
sections.what: Styles the case header box and also lists the other boxes, such as summary, form, inspection and issue cards, that take the same look as the summary card.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps content boxes visually consistent.
sections.watch_out: Every selector listed here receives the summary card look, so a new box added to this list will change its appearance too.

sections.name: .summary-card
sections.title: Summary card look
sections.what: Gives summary cards a translucent background, soft blur, rounded corners and padding.
sections.why: Likely reason: matches the other content boxes.
sections.watch_out: The selector list at the end of this block starts a new button group, so editing the boundary can change button looks.

sections.name: .button
sections.title: Main button style
sections.what: Styles the main call-to-action buttons with a dark fill, light text, rounded corners and a pointer cursor.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: .button.secondary
sections.title: Secondary button style
sections.what: Gives secondary buttons a lighter grey fill with dark text.
sections.why: Likely reason: secondary actions should look less prominent.

sections.name: .button:hover
sections.title: Button fade on hover
sections.what: Makes buttons slightly faded when the mouse is over them.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

summary: Stylesheet that sets the colours, spacing, fonts and layout for the app's pages, including light and dark themes and phone-sized layouts.
purpose: Controls how the app looks: colours, fonts, the side menu, the home hero, the map, case pages and buttons.
why: Likely reason: keeps the whole visual design in one place so every page shares the same look.
how: The file first sets the base colours and fonts, then the dark theme overrides, then styles for each part of the app grouped by area, and finally the screen-size rules at the end. When two rules match the same element, the one later in the file wins.
inputs: Class names and attributes set by the app's page code, such as the theme attribute on the root element and the width of the browser window.
outputs: Visual styling only. The file stores and returns no data.
risks: Several colours are set twice, once in the base block and again in the dark theme blocks, so a change in one place may not show in dark mode. Some selectors share one look unexpectedly, and some layer controls are hidden by a later rule.
debug: Use the browser's inspector on an element to see which rule is winning. Check the theme attribute on the root element. Compare the browser width with the breakpoints at 700, 860 and 1100 pixels.
